newsitem.title: FINLAND: PROTOS SEES FINNISH TENDER RATE RISE BEFORE END-96.
newsitem.headline: PROTOS SEES FINNISH TENDER RATE RISE BEFORE END-96.

text.p: Finnish brokerage Davy Protos Stockbrokers is expecting a hike in the Bank of Finland's key tender rate before the end of 1996, it said in a weekly report.
"The tender rate will rise before the turn of the year," Protos economist Petteri Hirvonen wrote in the report.
"It is quite clear that a rise in short-term interest rates will not turn the economy into a decline," he said, referring to a multitude of factors boosting growth.
"... growth can continue for years as long as it is not allowed to accelerate too strongly," he said.
A rise in short-term interest rates through a tender rate hike would at most slightly slow down growth, he added.
"The most important effect that a rise now in short-term interest rates will have is the signal that the central bank will not let inflation speed up in the next few years," Hirvonen said.

Protos gave no forecast for by how much it expected the tender rate to be raised. Currently, the tender rate, the Bank of Finland's chief monetary policy tool, is at 3.00 percent -- on par with the German Bundesbank's repo rate.
